product.title: Tin Can
product.description: A safe, screen-free WiFi landline phone for kids with limited, controlled calling and free party line access.

dossier.headline: The Landline Reinvented For Kids
dossier.summary: Tin Can is a screen-free, WiFi-enabled landline-style home phone for children, made by the Seattle-based company Tin Can and sold as hardware for about $100. It connects to home WiFi through a parent-managed companion app, allows calls only to approved contacts, and includes free party line access, positioning it as an alternative to giving kids smartphones.

story.title: The landline, reinvented for kids
story.detail: Tin Can markets a WiFi-enabled, screen-free phone that only calls approved contacts, with no display, apps, texting, games, or web browser. It connects to home WiFi through a parent-managed companion app rather than a traditional phone jack.

story.title: A viral word-of-mouth hit
story.detail: Launched in April 2025, Tin Can became a word-of-mouth success among families in the US and Canada, with reporting citing hundreds of thousands of units sold and early batches repeatedly selling out at $100.

story.title: Broad parenting-press coverage
story.detail: Wirecutter (The New York Times), PureWow, Domino, and Parade published reviews highlighting the phone's screen-free design and controlled contact list, with a four-month long-term test emphasizing its home-bound WiFi connection.

references.title: Kite Phone
references.detail: A UK guide compares Tin Can directly with Kite Phone, contrasting Tin Can's home-bound WiFi landline with Kite's mobile offering and subscription model.

references.title: Minimalist 'dumb phones' for families
references.detail: Coverage positions Tin Can alongside minimalist phones marketed to families who want connectivity without app ecosystems.

references.title: VoIP home phones
references.detail: Business coverage compares Tin Can to a VoIP home phone with strong parental controls, framing it as a smartphone alternative for kids.

dossier.lookbookStyle: Bright, clean home-lifestyle photography with soft natural daylight, warm neutral palette, uncluttered domestic sets, and a cheerful screen-free family mood.
dossier.lookbookPrompt: A single editorial lookbook sheet as one 3:2 landscape image, arranged as a strict 2x2 grid (2 rows x 2 columns) of four landscape photographs, identical cell sizes, uniform hairline gutters, grid flush to all four edges with no outer margin. Cell 1 (top-left): the retro-red Tin Can kids landline phone on a bright kitchen counter, straight-on angle. Cell 2 (top-right): close crop of a child's hand lifting the corded handset. Cell 3 (bottom-left): the phone base plugged in on a tidy desk nook with a WiFi router nearby. Cell 4 (bottom-right): the whole phone on an entryway table in soft morning light. In each cell frame the phone to fill about two thirds of the frame. Vary pose, crop, angle and setting between cells; all share bright, clean home-lifestyle photography with soft natural daylight and a warm neutral palette. No text, captions, numbers, watermarks, rounded corners or drop shadows.
